items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: I played Carnegie Hall with that band... I said, “how are you going to get me” — he said, “we’ll get you on an airplane.” They took me from the airport to the stage to play with that band.

ctx.x: What were the toughest economic years for you, as far as gigs?

I don’t remember. Well Eddie Condon’s closed in 1985. Both of my sons graduated from high school in 1985 and went to college in 1985. And there was a little lull in there that was a little nerve wracking. But my one son, the bassist, got a full paid scholarship to the Boston Conservatory, so that helped. The other one went to Manhattan School of Music and then decided he wanted to become a physicist so that took care of that. And I was working various jobs in New York and then Anita O’Day came into the game. And…
